evidence.decision: Person Domain v2 Military audit. Re-review all 209 live military Persons against the active eight-sector taxonomy using representative historical identity. Military remains the home of warfare, military command and armed leadership when those are the durable representative identity. A governing office or ruler title does not by itself force governance when the historical identity is overwhelmingly military, but clear long-duration sovereign rulership remains governance under the established ATLAS top-state rule. Preserve explicit prior user-adjudicated military boundary decisions unless stronger current evidence contradicts them.

edge_case_notes.basis: Pyrrhus was not merely a field commander: he repeatedly exercised sovereign kingship in Epirus and Macedon across much of his adult career. Under the established ATLAS rule that a clear secular top ruler remains governance even when also a celebrated general, his durable representative identity crosses the military/governance boundary in favor of governance.

Sviatoslav was Grand Prince of Kyiv, de jure from 945 and de facto from the 960s until 972, and his conquests were conducted as the sovereign ruler expanding Kyivan Rus. His military reputation is exceptional, but the warfare is inseparable from his direct top-state rulership; under the ATLAS top-state rule governance is the stronger single representative domain.

Skanderbeg also ruled the Kastrioti principality, but standard historical framing centers his durable identity on armed resistance and military leadership against the Ottoman Empire. Unlike a monarch whose historical representation is primarily dynastic rule, his princely authority and war leadership are effectively the same resistance career, so military remains representative.

Nuku became Sultan of Tidore, but his representative historical identity is the long anti-Dutch Nuku resistance movement from 1780 until his death; the sultanate phase was the political culmination of that armed struggle. Military therefore remains stronger than title-only reassignment.

Wellington twice served as prime minister, but the UK government's own historical profile states that he is today more famous as a soldier than as a politician. His durable representative identity therefore remains military.

Mannerheim served as regent and president, but Finnish official/public-history sources foreground his career as military commander, commander-in-chief and national war hero. The later presidency does not outweigh the military identity for this single representative code.
Preserve the explicit user-adjudicated governance-to-military correction already recorded in PR #1162; the revolt leadership is the controlling representative-domain decision.

Preserve the reviewed Batch 040 decision in PR #1023, which explicitly found that Tecumseh does not trigger the sovereign/top-state governance override and that his durable identity is military/wartime leadership.

Preserve the completed Religion audit decision in PR #1911 that moved Lalla Fatma from religion to military because anti-colonial resistance leadership outweighs religion as the single representative domain.
Preserve the explicit reviewed military assignment in PR #1629 for the ǀXam leadership/resistance interval.

Dufour was also a structural engineer and topographer, but he held the Swiss office of General and commanded the federal army in the Sonderbund War. His cross-domain engineering/cartographic significance is substantial but does not clearly outweigh the national military-command identity, so no move is justified.

Although Lakshmibai was the Rani of Jhansi and exercised leadership, her durable historical representation is as a leading armed figure of the 1857 rebellion who personally fought the British. The military identity is therefore stronger than title-only governance reassignment.
